notes:
Summary: Catalyze is a mid-market UX & product analytics SaaS (B2B) that wants to migrate core LLM inference from their current provider (OpenAI API) to Redwood. Motivation: better cost predictability at scale, deterministic latency for support chat SLAs, and vendor flexibility. They want to use Redwood Hosted for a fast POC, then move to Dedicated for steady-state traffic and reserved capacity.

Key requirements:
- Workloads: conversational support assistant (multi-turn), embeddings for doc search, and reranking for personalized recommendations.
- Latency/throughput: 95th percentile latency target <= 350ms for chat path; peak throughput ~120 reqs/s for support during US business hours; embeddings batch jobs overnight (~10k docs/day).
- Cost sensitivity: tight unit-cost targets, want batching and caching recommendations; looking to compare token-based hosted pricing vs their current spend.
- Model constraints: prefer open-model variants compatible with current prompts; must preserve prompt parity (system prompts, stop tokens, temperature) to avoid regressions. 

Migration notes / POC findings:
- Integration: SDK integration completed in staging within 3 days; most endpoints mapped to Redwood Hosted with small adapter shim (200 lines) to keep compatibility with existing OpenAI-style client calls.
- Prompt parity: engineering team discovered differences in default system-token behavior and whitespace trimming which affected reranker scores. SE-led prompt normalization tests reduced divergence by ~60%.
- Regressions: reranking precision dip (~4-6% on benchmark set) when switching model family; flagged as highest priority. We proposed: controlled A/B with model fallback policy + grading harness.
- Observability: Redwood Console trace hooks were useful; request-level token counts helped identify unexpected prompt bloat.

Security & compliance: they require SSO (SAML) and audit logs; legal pushed for data residency guarantees for EU customers (current partial). They asked about KMS integration and customer-managed keys; Redwood capabilities demoed by SE.

Commercial/Procurement: Catalyze prefers starting hosted (low friction) to validate parity and performance, then sign a 12–24m Dedicated commit for reserved GPU pools. AE provided a draft TCO comparing current spend to Redwood Dedicated at 20% lower estimated unit cost.

Quotes & paraphrases from meetings:
- "We need prompt parity — our support SLAs can't take regressions overnight."
- "If Dedicated saves us >15% on unit cost, legal and procurement are much more comfortable."

Immediate next steps: finish regression triage, run a 2-week A/B rerank experiment (golden prompt set), detailed Dedicated sizing session with infra + finance, and security KMS/residency doc.
